caveats: ⚑ burst weaponSwap shot economy: kit states only damagePct 33% + 7 sec. No maxAmmo, pullsPerSec, weapon class or chargeTime given — the swap inherits the base MG cadence (300 ammo, 171 reloadFrames) by omission. If the swap weapon is not an MG, shot count over the 7 sec window is wrong. MEASUREMENT-GATED.

⚑ burst Fire-Code rider cadence: 'when attacking a Fire Code target' names the CONDITION but not the per-hit cadence; modeled as per-trigger-pull (shotFired). If it is per-HIT (MG hitsPerShot 1 here, so identical) or on an internal cooldown, the rate is wrong. Also unstated whether it is burst-window-scoped or whole-fight — modeled as whole-fight (the header carries no duration).
⚑ skill1 partsDamagePct is engine-inert at scope lock (partless boss). Kept for kit completeness per the tandem/completeness rule; contributes zero damage on the graded comps.

⚑ escalating counters are per-battle and never reset in the kit text; steps 2 and 3 of each skill are cumulative ADDS on top of step 1 (Liter-style 'each subsequent effect triggers all effects before it'), giving 12.4/24.8/37.2 and 20.56/40.76/60.96 at the 1st/2nd/3rd activation.
⚑ cadence tuple (pullsPerSec / reloadFrames 171 / ammo 300) is datamine-sourced and known-unreliable; not independently verified.
override.note: PARSER BASELINE (HYPOTHESIS — NOT a validated model). Every ⚑ below is an UNMEASURED estimate; hand-tune + record against a real fight before trusting any number. Neon: Blue Ocean is MG/Water/Attacker/Burst III. S1 is a burst-cast-keyed escalating Damage-to-Parts stack (inert vs the partless scope-lock boss but modeled for completeness). S2 is a stageEnter{3} escalating Elemental Advantage Attack Damage buff — modeled as elemAdvantageDamagePct so it lands in the Damage Up bucket and is live only with elemental advantage (taxonomy item 8: this kit exceeds the clean x1.10). Trigger fidelity: S2 says 'entering Burst Stage 3', which is a STAGE entry any team B3 cast satisfies, NOT full-burst-enter and NOT self-burst-cast; keying it to burstCast would under-fire in comps where another B3 casts, keying it to fullBurstEnter would shift it past the stage boundary. Burst is a 7 sec weapon swap at 33% of final ATK plus a boss-element-gated 11%-of-final-ATK rider on Fire Code targets, authored target enemy with bossElementGate 'Fire' so it is inert vs the neutral scope-lock boss and never disturbs graded comps. Every kit line is IMPLEMENTED; unmodeled is empty for all three slots.

flags.estimate: swap inherits base MG cadence + 300 ammo + 171 reloadFrames; ~7 sec of uninterrupted MG fire at 33%/shot
flags.reasoning: ALWAYS-⚑ #3: weapon-swap shot economy is kit-silent. The kit gives ONLY damagePct and duration — no maxAmmo, no pullsPerSec, no weapon class, no chargeTime, no maxShots. Omitting those fields makes the engine reuse the base MG spec, which is the optimistic read (an MG belt of 300 will not empty in 7 sec, so no reload interrupts the window). If the swap is actually a different weapon class or a lower-capacity weapon, both shot count and range-band/core behaviour change.
flags.recipe: Focus-camera recording of her burst window: count trigger pulls between the burst banner and the swap ending (~7 sec later), and read the ammo counter at swap start/end. Shots-per-second from the ammo delta directly settles pullsPerSec (the ammo counter measures the DISPUTED quantity; FB counts do not). Popup colour/size settles whether swap shots core.

flags.estimate: shotFired — one 11%-of-final-ATK instance per trigger pull, whole-fight, gated on a Fire boss
flags.reasoning: ALWAYS-⚑ #2: the kit gives an activation CONDITION ('when attacking a Fire Code target') but no cadence, no internal cooldown, and no duration. shotFired is the literal reading of 'when attacking'. Base hitsPerShot is 1, so per-pull and per-hit coincide here and the ambiguity costs nothing at base — but it WOULD diverge if the burst swap weapon has hitsPerShot > 1. Also unstated: whether the rider is scoped to the 7 sec burst window (it sits in the burst slot under its own header) or is a whole-fight passive. Modeled whole-fight because the header carries no duration; if it is actually swap-scoped, add swapGate 'swapped'.
flags.recipe: Requires a FIRE-code boss recording (the scope-lock boss is neutral, so this block is inert on every graded comp and cannot be measured there). On a Fire boss: count 11%-value popups against her trigger pulls over a fixed window, and check whether they stop when the 7 sec swap ends. Until such a recording exists this rider is unfalsifiable at scope lock — which is also why it is safe to land.

flags.field: override.skill2[0] trigger identity (stageEnter{3} vs fullBurstEnter vs burstCast)
flags.reasoning: Taxonomy item 3 (TRIGGER IDENTITY) is the highest-value call in this kit. 'Activates when entering Burst Stage 3' names the ROTATION STAGE, not the Full Burst window and not this unit's own cast. As the sole B3 in a standard 1-2-3 comp the three readings mostly coincide, which is exactly the trap: they diverge in any comp with a second B3 (burstCast under-fires when the other B3 casts) and they diverge in timing by the measured 30f stage->stage / 22f->FB chain gap (fullBurstEnter lands the 10 sec window later, clipping its tail differently against a 10 sec FB). Since this unit IS a B3, note also that her own burst cast satisfies stageEnter{3}, so S1 (burstCast) and S2 (stageEnter 3) fire near-simultaneously on her own rotations but decouple on rotations she sits out.
flags.recipe: Two-B3 comp (this unit + another B3, only one casting per rotation): sim A/B the three trigger readings and compare per-unit damage against a focus recording. Directly: a buffApply-event assertion in scripts/tests/units/neon-blue-ocean.test.ts counting elemAdvantageDamagePct applications per rotation — stageEnter{3} fires on every rotation, burstCast only on rotations she bursts.

flags.reasoning: Taxonomy item 8: element advantage is normally a clean x1.10, but 'Elemental Advantage Attack Damage ▲' is precisely the kit line that makes it exceed x1.10, so it must be modeled rather than folded into the element constant. The stat is scoped — it must contribute to the Damage Up bucket ONLY when the attacker actually holds elemental advantage. This unit is Water; against the neutral scope-lock boss she has NO advantage, so the whole S2 chain is INERT at scope lock and this is a Fire-boss-only buff. That inertness is load-bearing for the reading of any graded comp: S2 contributes zero there, and a board reading cannot validate it.
flags.recipe: Confirm scoping with a sim A/B on a FIRE boss vs the neutral boss with S2 present/absent: the delta must be zero on neutral and positive on Fire. Cross-check the Damage Up bucket placement against docs/data/damage-calculation.md rather than re-deriving it.

flags.estimate: buff retained at 12.4/24.8/37.2 cumulative; zero damage contribution in v1
flags.reasoning: The scope-lock boss is PARTLESS (a verified project fact), and partsDamagePct is parsed-but-inert. Skipping the line would be the taxonomy-4 error (dropping a line because it is inert in isolation); keeping it costs nothing and preserves kit completeness for a future parts-capable boss. Consequence worth stating plainly: skill1 AND skill2 are BOTH inert at scope lock, so this unit's entire modeled non-burst kit contributes nothing on the graded comps — her sim damage there is base MG fire plus the 7 sec swap alone.
flags.recipe: No measurement needed for the inertness itself (it follows from the partless-boss fact + the stat's v1 status). If parts modeling ever lands, re-verify the escalating cumulative shape against a parts-bearing fight.

flags.reasoning: ALWAYS-⚑ #1: rate_of_fire and reloadFrames are known-unreliable datamine fields, and a nominal rate is not the effective rate — the game fires on 60fps frame boundaries, so effective = 60/ceil(60/nominal). An MG additionally carries the measured wind-up/wind-down ladder, which dominates short windows like a 7 sec swap. Not independently verified here; flagged rather than asserted.
flags.recipe: Ammo-counter read from a focus recording (shots/sec measured directly) rather than any FB-count-derived inference, which is downstream of gauge and cannot settle cadence.
